title.narrative: Strengthening DRM and Climate Resilience Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve: (i) early warning and emergency evacuation capacity in selected municipalities in high climate risk-prone areas; (ii) the provision of and accessibility to safe havens; and (iii) the GoH's capacity to respond to an eligible emergency.

The development objective of Strengthening Disaster Risk Management and Climate Resilience Project for Haiti is to improve: (i) early warning and emergency evacuation capacity in selected municipalities in high climate risk-prone areas, and (ii) the provision of and accessibility to safe havens. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Strengthening Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Response Capacity and Promoting Building Regulation and Resilient Construction Practices, comprises two sub-components: (i) Strengthening Disaster Preparedness, and Emergency Response Capacity, and Disaster Risk Data Management, and (ii) Promoting Building Regulations and Resilient Construction Practices at the Local Level. 2) The second component, Construction and Rehabilitation of Safe Havens aims to finance: (a) the construction, reconstruction and/or rehabilitation of selected emergency shelters or safe havens, including those in schools, community centers, markets, and roadside annexes, and the reinforcement of small road infrastructure acting as emergency walkways leading to safe havens, prioritized according to the methodology; (b) the provision of improved basic services to these safe havens (compliant with climate change mitigation approaches); (c) technical studies, including relevant engineering designs, technical audits, social and environmental safeguard instruments, and shelter activation and closure operating procedures for selected investments; (d) training, technical assistance and communication activities aimed at achieving social mobilization and coordination of safe haven's investments among all stakeholders participating in the Project; and (e) monitoring and supervision of works. 3) The third component, Contingent Emergency Response, aims to finance the implementation of emergency works, rehabilitation, and associated assessments in the event of a natural disaster. 4) The fourth component, Project Management and Implementation Support, aims to finance the costs related to overall project management and implementation support.

title.narrative: Number of CCPCs with a refreshed training and improved competencies in emergency planning and management – Minimum with a Level 2 certification

comment.narrative:
This indicator has been fully achieved. As noted under the PDO indicator, the final competency assessment of the Municipal Civil Protection Committees (CCPCs) was completed at the end of April 2026.
The results indicate that 115 CCPCs have achieved at least Level 2 (Good) certification in emergency planning and management. The assessment was based on six key criteria: participation in training, receipt of emergency equipment, availability of an operational Emergency Operations Center (EOC), existence of an updated and tested contingency plan, involvement of local authorities, and regular committee meetings.
Each CCPC was evaluated across four certification levels: Level 1 – Excellent; Level 2 – Good; Level 3 – Average; and Level 4 – Weak.

The assessment was based on six key criteria: participation in training, receipt of emergency equipment, existence of an operational EOC, an updated and tested contingency plan, involvement of local authorities, and regular committee meetings. Each CCPC was rated according to four certification levels: Level 1 – Excellent | Level 2 – Good | Level 3 – Average | Level 4 – Weak.

title.narrative: Development of protocols for National Early Warning Service and Communication System for Hydromet events approved and adopted.

comment.narrative: The National Reference Plan for Early Warning Systems in Haiti, together with three specific alert management plans for cyclones, heavy rainfall and related impacts, and coastal waves and flooding, were validated during a joint DGPC–UHM workshop in March 2025. They were implemented for the first time during Hurricane Melissa in October 2025, significantly improving inter-institutional coordination and alert management in Haiti, thereby fully meeting the indicator.

title.narrative: Increase in the number of people living in flood-risk areas who have access to a safe haven.

comment.narrative:
The value of this indicator has been updated since the last ISR to reflect a revised calculation methodology and the inclusion of additional infrastructure supported under the project. Following the rehabilitation of five schools in the Nippes department in 2022, designated for use as temporary shelters, and the subsequent rehabilitation of one additional school in the Nippes department in January 2026 under the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC), a total of 10,686 people living in flood-prone areas are now considered to have access to safe shelter. Of this total, approximately 5,343 beneficiaries are women (50%).
In parallel, construction of additional shelters by the Delegated Implementing Agencies (MDOD) is progressing. Currently, 20 shelters are under construction. Once finalized, this indicator will be updated.

title.narrative: Number of rehabilitated or improved DGPC's Emergency Operation Centers by the project

comment.narrative: This indicator has been fully achieved. All rehabilitation works planned for the eight Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs) affected by the August 2021 earthquake have been completed. These include three Departmental Emergency Operations Centers (COUD) in FondfrEde, Miragoâne, and JErEmie, and five Communal Emergency Operations Centers (COUC) in Camp-Perrin, Les Côteaux, Aquin, Fond-des-NEgres, and ChardonniEres. The recently rehabilitated COUD in JErEmie, along with the COUCs in ChardonniEres, Les Côteaux, and Camp-Perrin, were officially inaugurated by local authorities in February 2026.
